summary: Started S026 (WTI Crude Oil, EIA event volatility, Confluence P12/S025+S026+S027 page 24838145) with the piece the spec itself flags as the biggest non-statistical risk: the exact EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report release calendar (Wednesday 10:30am ET default, shifts around holidays). Fetched the live schedule (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php) and verified a general rule against all 14 published holiday-shift rows (2024-12..2026-11): if a US federal holiday (holidays package, US calendar) falls on the Mon/Tue/Wed of the normal release week, EIA delays Wed->Thu -- matches 13/14 rows exactly. The 14th (week ending 2025-12-19, released 2025-12-29 Monday, not a simple +1 day) is a genuinely irregular year-end production gap that is NOT rule-derivable -- kept as an explicit, dated KNOWN_HOLIDAY_SHIFTS override table (all 14 rows, source-linked, dated 2026-09-23 fetch) rather than guessed at. eia_release_datetime() checks the table first, falls back to the verified general rule, and RAISES UnregisteredYearEndShiftError (does not guess) for any future December/January week whose default Wednesday lands within 2 days of Christmas or New Year's Day and isn't yet registered -- confirmed this guard correctly flags all 14 such weeks 2015-2026 in the runner check below (12 pre-dating this table's coverage, 2 right at its edges). 23 tests in tests/strategies/test_eia_calendar.py (all 14 published rows individually, the general-rule-alone reproduction, the raise-not-guess behavior, ordinary weeks). Full tests/strategies+utils suite (100 tests) green. Then wrote backtest/run_eia_calendar_check.py -- NOT a backtest, a data-availability check -- which found the actual, hard blocker: yfinance only serves ~60-70 calendar days of intraday (15m/30m/1h) CL=F history (a Yahoo platform limit), vs. ~51 EIA events/year -- at most 8-9 usable historical events, far below even the spec's own already-flagged-as-thin ~50/year concern. No backtest was run or fabricated on this insufficient sample. Documented two real paths forward, neither attempted (both need Anton's explicit go-ahead): (1) cTrader Open API historical trendbars -- bot/ctrader_orb.py, ctrader_s007.py, ctrader_s011.py already use ProtoOAGetTrendbarsReq against the live demo account for other CFDs; if the broker has an oil CFD with deep minute history, same pattern, new symbol, but touches live broker credentials so not wired up here; (2) start a forward-only collector now (same irrecoverability logic as the Deribit options-snapshot job in infra-scheduled-jobs-spec.md), accepting a usable sample is a year+ away. S026 status: calendar infrastructure built and tested, backtest blocked on data, explicitly not faked.

Documented the S026 calendar + data-availability finding (see preceding entry) in Confluence per confluence-docs, via the REST-API fallback (.env creds, device_bash), same mechanism used for S025/S027. Updated 'P12 / S025+S026+S027' page id 24838145 (v4->v5): inserted a dated subsection under the S026 heading with the calendar verification summary and a note macro stating plainly that no backtest exists and why (yfinance intraday CL=F ~60-70 day limit), plus the two real paths forward. Appended a row to 'Апдейты (журнал работ)' page id 10584066 (v6->v7).
